title: Define the Three Primary Trigonometric Ratios
text: Define the three primary trigonometric ratios: sine (sin), cosine (cos), and tangent (tan) in terms of opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse of a right triangle.
options: sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj
sin θ = Opp/Adj, cos θ = Adj/Opp, tan θ = Hyp/Adj
sin θ = Adj/Hyp, cos θ = Opp/Hyp, tan θ = Hyp/Opp
sin θ = Hyp/Opp, cos θ = Hyp/Adj, tan θ = Adj/Opp
answer: sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj
hint: SOH-CAH-TOA: Sine is Opp/Hyp, Cosine is Adj/Hyp, Tangent is Opp/Adj.
steps: **Final Answer:** sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj

title: State the Mnemonic SOH-CAH-TOA
text: State the mnemonic SOH-CAH-TOA and explain its meaning in right triangle trigonometry.
options: SOH: sin = Opp/Hyp, CAH: cos = Adj/Hyp, TOA: tan = Opp/Adj
SOH: sin = Opp/Adj, CAH: cos = Adj/Opp, TOA: tan = Hyp/Adj
SOH: sin = Adj/Hyp, CAH: cos = Opp/Hyp, TOA: tan = Opp/Adj
SOH: sin = Hyp/Opp, CAH: cos = Hyp/Adj, TOA: tan = Adj/Opp
answer: SOH: sin = Opp/Hyp, CAH: cos = Adj/Hyp, TOA: tan = Opp/Adj
hint: SOH stands for Sine = Opposite / Hypotenuse.
steps: **Step 1: Parse SOH** - S = Sine, O = Opposite, H = Hypotenuse.
**Step 2: Parse CAH** - C = Cosine, A = Adjacent, H = Hypotenuse.
**Step 3: Parse TOA** - T = Tangent, O = Opposite, A = Adjacent.
**Final Answer:** SOH: sin = Opp/Hyp, CAH: cos = Adj/Hyp, TOA: tan = Opp/Adj

title: Trigonometric Ratios for 3-4-5 Right Triangle
text: In right triangle ABC with right angle at C, side a = 3, b = 4, and c = 5. Write the exact numerical values of sin A, cos A, tan A, sin B, cos B, and tan B.
options: sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4, sin B = 4/5, cos B = 3/5, tan B = 4/3
sin A = 4/5, cos A = 3/5, tan A = 4/3, sin B = 3/5, cos B = 4/5, tan B = 3/4
sin A = 3/4, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/5, sin B = 4/3, cos B = 3/5, tan B = 4/5
sin A = 5/3, cos A = 5/4, tan A = 4/3, sin B = 5/4, cos B = 5/3, tan B = 3/4
answer: sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4, sin B = 4/5, cos B = 3/5, tan B = 4/3
hint: For angle A, opposite is a = 3, adjacent is b = 4, hypotenuse c = 5.
steps: **Step 1: Calculate ratios for A** - sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4.
**Step 2: Calculate ratios for B** - sin B = 4/5, cos B = 3/5, tan B = 4/3.
**Final Answer:** sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4, sin B = 4/5, cos B = 3/5, tan B = 4/3

title: Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios Definitions
text: Define the reciprocal trigonometric ratios: cosecant (csc), secant (sec), and cotangent (cot) in terms of sine, cosine, and tangent.
options: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ
csc θ = 1/cos θ, sec θ = 1/sin θ, cot θ = tan θ
csc θ = sin θ, sec θ = cos θ, cot θ = tan θ
csc θ = 1/tan θ, sec θ = 1/sin θ, cot θ = 1/cos θ
answer: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ
hint: Cosecant is reciprocal of sine; secant is reciprocal of cosine.
steps: **Final Answer:** csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ

title: Co-Function Trigonometric Identities
text: State the co-function identities relating sine and cosine, and tangent and cotangent for complementary acute angles.
options: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, cos(90° - θ) = sin θ, tan(90° - θ) = cot θ
sin(90° - θ) = sin θ, cos(90° - θ) = cos θ, tan(90° - θ) = tan θ
sin(90° + θ) = cos θ, cos(90° + θ) = sin θ, tan(90° + θ) = cot θ
sin(180° - θ) = cos θ, cos(180° - θ) = sin θ, tan(180° - θ) = cot θ
answer: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, cos(90° - θ) = sin θ, tan(90° - θ) = cot θ
hint: Co-functions of complementary angles are equal.
steps: **Final Answer:** sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, cos(90° - θ) = sin θ, tan(90° - θ) = cot θ

title: Define Angle of Elevation
text: Define an angle of elevation and select its correct geometric description.
formula: \text{Angle of Elevation} = \text{Angle between line of sight and horizontal looking UPWARD}
options: Angle formed by line of sight and horizontal when looking UPWARD
Angle formed by line of sight and horizontal when looking DOWNWARD
Angle formed by line of sight and vertical wall
Angle formed by ground and vertical wall
answer: Angle formed by line of sight and horizontal when looking UPWARD
hint: Elevation refers to looking above the horizontal line of sight.
steps: **Step 1: Horizontal reference** - Line parallel to ground.
**Step 2: Upward sight** - Observer looks up to object.
**Final Answer:** Angle formed by line of sight and horizontal when looking UPWARD

title: Define Angle of Depression
text: Define an angle of depression and explain why the angle of depression from an observer to a target equals the angle of elevation from the target back to the observer.
formula: \text{Angle of Depression} = \text{Angle of Elevation (by Alternate Interior Angles)}
options: Looking DOWNWARD; equal by Alternate Interior Angles of parallel horizontals
Looking UPWARD; equal by Vertical Angles
Looking DOWNWARD; equal by Complementary Angles summing to 90°
Looking UPWARD; equal by Corresponding Angles
answer: Looking DOWNWARD; equal by Alternate Interior Angles of parallel horizontals
hint: Horizontal lines of sight at top and bottom are parallel.
steps: **Step 1: Downward sight** - Observer looks down below horizontal.
**Step 2: Parallel lines** - Horizontal lines at top and bottom are parallel.
**Step 3: Transversal** - Line of sight is a transversal forming equal alternate interior angles.
**Final Answer:** Looking DOWNWARD; equal by Alternate Interior Angles of parallel horizontals

title: Conceptual Bound: Why sin θ and cos θ Never Exceed 1
text: Explain why the value of sin θ and cos θ can never exceed 1 for any acute angle θ in a right triangle.
options: Hypotenuse is always the longest side, so ratio Opp/Hyp or Adj/Hyp ≤ 1
Legs are always equal to hypotenuse in all right triangles
Sum of acute angles is 180°, limiting ratio values
Pythagorean theorem restricts tangent values to 1
answer: Hypotenuse is always the longest side, so ratio Opp/Hyp or Adj/Hyp ≤ 1
hint: In any right triangle, the hypotenuse opposite 90° is strictly longer than either leg.
steps: **Step 1: Hypotenuse property** - Hypotenuse is the longest side in a right triangle.
**Step 2: Ratio upper bound** - Numerator (leg) is smaller than denominator (hypotenuse).
**Final Answer:** Hypotenuse is always the longest side, so ratio Opp/Hyp or Adj/Hyp ≤ 1

title: Conceptual Behavior: Why tan θ Grows Without Bound
text: Explain why tan θ increases without bound as θ approaches 90°.
options: As θ → 90°, Adjacent leg → 0, so Opp/Adj → ∞
As θ → 90°, Opposite leg → 0, so Adj/Opp → ∞
As θ → 90°, sum of angles exceeds 180°
answer: As θ → 90°, Adjacent leg → 0, so Opp/Adj → ∞
hint: As angle approaches 90°, adjacent leg shrinks toward 0 while opposite leg remains non-zero.
steps: **Step 1: Adjacent leg shrink** - Adj → 0 as θ → 90°.
**Step 2: Division by zero limit** - Opp / Adj → ∞.
**Final Answer:** As θ → 90°, Adjacent leg → 0, so Opp/Adj → ∞

title: Algebraic Trigonometric Expressions for sin θ = x/y
text: If sin θ = x / y, express cos θ and tan θ in terms of algebraic variables x and y for acute angle θ.
options: cos θ = √(y² - x²)/y, tan θ = x/√(y² - x²)
cos θ = x/√(y² + x²), tan θ = y/x
cos θ = (y - x)/y, tan θ = x/(y - x)
cos θ = √(x² + y²)/y, tan θ = √(y² - x²)/x
answer: cos θ = √(y² - x²)/y, tan θ = x/√(y² - x²)
hint: Opposite = x, Hypotenuse = y ⟹ Adjacent = √(y² - x²).
steps: **Step 2: cos θ** - Adjacent / Hypotenuse = √(y² - x²) / y
**Step 3: tan θ** - Opposite / Adjacent = x / √(y² - x²)
**Final Answer:** cos θ = √(y² - x²)/y, tan θ = x/√(y² - x²)

title: Prove Identity tan θ + cot θ = sec θ csc θ
text: Prove the trigonometric identity: tan θ + cot θ = sec θ csc θ for acute angles.
options: sin/cos + cos/sin = (sin² + cos²)/(sin cos) = 1/(sin cos) = sec csc
answer: sin/cos + cos/sin = (sin² + cos²)/(sin cos) = 1/(sin cos) = sec csc
hint: Convert to sines and cosines: sin/cos + cos/sin = (sin² + cos²)/(sin cos) = 1/(sin cos).
steps: **Step 1: Common denominator** - (sin² θ + cos² θ) / (sin θ cos θ)
**Step 2: Apply Pythagorean identity** - 1 / (sin θ cos θ)
**Step 3: Convert to reciprocals** - (1/cos θ)(1/sin θ) = sec θ csc θ
**Final Answer:** sin/cos + cos/sin = (sin² + cos²)/(sin cos) = 1/(sin cos) = sec csc

title: Prove Identity (1 - sin θ)(1 + sin θ) = cos² θ
text: Prove that (1 - sin θ)(1 + sin θ) = cos² θ.
hint: Difference of squares: (1 - sin θ)(1 + sin θ) = 1 - sin² θ = cos² θ.
steps: **Step 1: Expand difference of squares** - 1 - sin² θ
**Step 2: Apply Pythagorean identity** - cos² θ = 1 - sin² θ
